stops.title: Stop sending `*` together with credentials
stops.body: With `cors({ origin: '*', credentials: true })` the middleware used to send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` along with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, and browsers reject that pair. The PR changes the wildcard case: when `credentials` is set, the middleware now echoes back the request's `Origin`, and it adds `Vary: Origin`.

stops.title: One resolver branch and two Vary conditions
stops.body: `findAllowOrigin` is built once per `cors()` call, based on `opts.origin`. The request handler calls it at line 109 and sets the header if the result is truthy. `Vary: Origin` is set in two places: on the preflight path (OPTIONS) and after `next()` for normal requests. The PR touches all three spots, and `index.test.ts` adds a new `/api10/*` route to test them.

stops.title: Wildcard plus credentials now echoes any Origin
stops.body: When `optsOrigin === '*'` and `opts.credentials` is truthy, the resolver returns `origin || null`. Any non-empty request `Origin`, including the literal `'null'`, gets echoed back while `Allow-Credentials: true` is also sent. In practice, any website can now make credentialed requests and read the responses. Before, the browser blocked those reads because of the `*`. `origin` defaults to `'*'` (line 65), so passing only `credentials: true` also turns on this behavior. Express's `cors` package keeps sending `*` when `origin: '*'`; it only echoes the origin when `origin: true`.

flags.note: Wildcard plus credentials now lets every origin (including the `null` origin from sandboxed pages) read credentialed responses, and a config that only sets `credentials: true` is affected too.
The description says this matches Express cors, but Express cors sends `*` for `origin: '*'` and only echoes the origin for `origin: true`.

stops.title: `Vary: Origin` added for the credentials case
stops.body: Both Vary conditions change from `opts.origin !== '*'` to `opts.origin !== '*' || opts.credentials`. Because the header value now depends on the request's origin, caches have to key on it. Preflight uses `set` (it replaces the header), while normal responses use `append: true`. This matches how the code already handled non-wildcard origins.

stops.title: Tests on the new `/api10` route
stops.body: A new `/api10/*` route uses `origin: '*', credentials: true`. The tests check four things: a normal GET echoes the origin and sets `Vary: Origin`; a preflight echoes it and `Vary` includes Origin; with no Origin header, no Allow-Origin is sent but Allow-Credentials still is; and two different origins each get echoed. The `Origin: null` test expects `'null'` to be echoed with credentials, so that behavior is now locked in by a test.

stops.title: Should a wildcard silently become “echo everyone”?
stops.body: Is it acceptable for `origin: '*'` with `credentials: true` (or just `credentials: true`, since `'*'` is the default) to automatically let every origin, including `null`, read credentialed responses? Or should this configuration keep failing in the browser, or require an explicit opt-in, like Express's `origin: true`?

question.text:
It returns `null`. When there's no `Origin` header, the middleware passes an empty string to the resolver (`c.req.header('origin') || ''`, line 109). In the wildcard-plus-credentials branch, `origin || null` turns that empty string into `null` (line 81).

Because the value is falsy, the `if (allowOrigin)` check at lines 110-112 skips it, so no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header is set. `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is still set, because that only depends on `opts.credentials` (lines 114-116).

For comparison, without credentials the `'*'` branch returns `'*'` no matter what the request sends (line 83). So in that case a request with no `Origin` still gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.
With credentials on, a request with no `Origin` header still gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, because the wildcard branch keeps returning `'*'` (line 81).
